papers.title: The effect of laser remelting on the surface chemistry of Ti6al4V components fabricated by selective laser melting
papers.abstract: Surface remelting/skin scanning of components is generally performed during the selective laser melting (SLM) process to improve the surface quality of a part. However, the chemical effects of surface remelting are not well understood. In this study, cuboidal parts fabricated with and without laser remelting were characterised using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), surface profilometry and X-ray photoelectron spectrophotometry (XPS). The SEM images showed a low-amplitude undulating pattern was observed on both surfaces. The surface chemistries of the surface remelted/skin scanned (SK) and non-surface remelted/non-skin scanned (NSK) samples were observed to significantly differ in their elemental composition. The thickness of the surface oxide layer of the SK surface was double that of the NSK surface. Also, the contribution of the major alloying elements, including titanium and aluminium, on the surface oxide layer varied for both NSK and SK surfaces. The surface chemistry of the NSK and SK surface was significantly different to a conventionally forged (CF) Ti6Al4V surface. The rate of decrease of oxide with depth was in the order of CF > NSK > SK. Although surface remelting is useful in rendering improved surface quality, its impact on surface chemistry should be carefully considered.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了选区激光熔化Ti6Al4V表面激光重熔的化学效应，未涉及应力遮挡或力学性能。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not cover stress shielding, mechanical testing, fatigue, or osseointegration; it focuses on surface chemistry only.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究SLM过程中激光重熔对Ti6Al4V表面化学的影响。
summary_zh.method: 制备重熔与非重熔的Ti6Al4V方块，通过SEM、轮廓仪和XPS表征表面。
summary_zh.result: 重熔后表面氧化层厚度增加一倍，元素组成与未重熔及锻造表面差异显著。
summary_zh.validation: 实验测量表面氧化物厚度和元素分布。

summary_en.motivation: To understand the chemical changes induced by laser remelting during selective laser melting of Ti6Al4V.
summary_en.method: Cuboidal samples were fabricated with and without laser remelting and characterized using SEM, profilometry, and XPS.
summary_en.result: Laser remelting doubled the surface oxide layer thickness and altered the elemental composition relative to non-remelted and forged surfaces.
summary_en.validation: Direct experimental measurement of surface oxide thickness and elemental composition.
